findings.message: The docs say an unlabelled blocker *or major* 'stays blocking in the round and at release'. In fast track, `_settle_round` (review_core.py) only blocks `severity == "blocker"`, so an unlabelled major goes to debt.md as `class:unclassified` and the round passes. Only the release gate blocks it. Fix the doc to say an unlabelled major blocks at release only, or make the fast-track filter block unclassified majors too.
findings.scenario: fast_track: all, finding {severity: major, no class} -> run exits 0, while SKILL.md says it stays blocking in the round

findings.message: `_release` verifies `<base>`/`<target>` once, then passes the symbolic ref to every later `git ls-tree`/`git show`. It never pins the resolved commit SHA, and the summary line prints only the ref names. If a branch moves mid-run, config and lists can come from different commits, and the output does not show which commits were gated. Resolve both refs to SHAs once, use those everywhere, and print them.

`CLASSES`, `DEFAULT_BLOCK_ON`, the class normaliser (`norm` vs `_class_token`) and the `release_gate.block_on` parser are second copies of the logic in review_core.py (`CLASSES`, `DEFAULT_BLOCK_ON`, `Config.block_on`). A parity test covers listed inputs, but the YAML handling differs (hand regex vs `parse_block`), so untested shapes can still diverge. Keep the parity table growing with each parser change, or share one module.

The `targetUrl` hard-codes `https://dev.azure.com/${AZDO_ORG}` and interpolates the branch and round path without URL-encoding. A `*.visualstudio.com` or on-prem collection, or a branch with `#`/`&`/space, yields a broken link on the posted status. The same unencoded `$HEAD_REF`/`${branch}` is used in specclaw-pr and github-actions.yml. Build the URL from the API base already in use, and quote the components.
